extra.title: Dockerfile missing user instruction
extra.message: The Dockerfile never sets a USER instruction, so the container runs as root by default. A process running as root that is compromised can more easily escalate to the host. Create and switch to an unprivileged user (e.g. RUN adduser -D app && USER app) before the container starts.

fix_info.hint: Create a non-root user and switch to it with a USER instruction so the container does not run as root.

extra.title: Cross-site scripting
extra.message: User input is written to the HTTP response (echo/print/printf) without output encoding, allowing reflected cross-site scripting. An attacker can inject HTML/JavaScript that runs in the victim's browser.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

fix_info.hint: Encode the value for its output context before printing it: htmlspecialchars($v, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') for HTML body/attributes (and additional JavaScript/URL encoding when reflecting into a <script> or a URL). In WordPress use the context escaper — esc_html() for element content, esc_attr() for attribute values, esc_url() for links, wp_kses_post() to keep a safe HTML subset. Prefer a templating engine that auto-escapes.

extra.title: File inclusion
extra.message: User input controls the path passed to include/require. An attacker can include local files (disclosing source or config) or, with a permissive configuration or wrapper, execute attacker-controlled code (LFI/RFI).

cwe: CWE-98: Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require Statement in PHP Program ('PHP Remote File Inclusion')

fix_info.hint: Map the request value to a fixed allowlist of permitted files and include only the resolved entry. If a directory must be dynamic, reduce the input with basename() and prefix a constant, trusted base path; never pass raw request data to include/require.

contract.strategy: Map the request value to a fixed allowlist of permitted files and include only the resolved entry. If a directory must be dynamic, reduce the input with basename() and prefix a constant, trusted base path; never pass raw request data to include/require.

extra.title: Object injection
extra.message: Untrusted data is passed to unserialize(). PHP instantiates the encoded objects and runs their magic methods (__wakeup, __destruct), so an attacker who controls the serialized string can trigger PHP Object Injection and, with a suitable gadget chain, remote code execution.

fix_info.hint: Do not unserialize untrusted input. Use json_decode() for data interchange. If unserialize() is unavoidable, pass the options ['allowed_classes' => false] (or an explicit class allowlist) — note that 'allowed_classes' => true still allows object injection.
